canonical_statement: The review objective was to determine the efficacy and safety of cannabinoids for the treatment of dementia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To determine the efficacy and safety of cannabinoids for the treatment of dementia.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had diagnosed dementia of any subtype or unspecified dementia, of any severity, from any setting, without age or sex restriction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included participants of any age and of either sex with diagnosed dementia of any subtype or with unspecified dementia of any severity from any setting.

population.label: People with diagnosed dementia of any subtype or severity
inclusion_criteria: Diagnosed dementia of any subtype or unspecified dementia

canonical_statement: The review included randomized controlled trials of cannabinoids for treatment of dementia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included all randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of cannabinoids for the treatment of dementia.

canonical_statement: Eligible cannabinoid interventions could use any route, dose, or duration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We considered studies of cannabinoids administered by any route, at any dose, for any duration, compared with placebo, no treatment, or any active control intervention.

canonical_statement: Eligible comparators were placebo, no treatment, or any active control intervention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We considered studies of cannabinoids administered by any route, at any dose, for any duration, compared with placebo, no treatment, or any active control intervention.

concept.text: Placebo, no treatment, or active control

canonical_statement: Primary outcomes included global and specific cognitive function.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary outcomes in this review were changes in global and specific cognitive function, overall behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD), and adverse events.

canonical_statement: Primary outcomes included overall behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary outcomes in this review were changes in global and specific cognitive function, overall behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD), and adverse events.

concept.text: Overall behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia

canonical_statement: Primary outcomes included adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary outcomes in this review were changes in global and specific cognitive function, overall behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD), and adverse events.

canonical_statement: The authors searched ALOIS on 8 July 2021 using cannabinoid-related terms; ALOIS incorporates major healthcare databases, trial registries, and grey-literature sources.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We searched ALOIS - the Cochrane Dementia and Cognitive Improvement Group’s Specialised Register - on 8 July 2021, using the terms cannabis or cannabinoid or endocannabinoid or cannabidiol or THC or CBD or dronabinol or delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol or marijuana or marihuana or hashish.

canonical_statement: Two review authors independently screened and selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias, with other authors involved for consensus when needed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two review authors independently screened and selected studies for inclusion, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias in included studies. When necessary, other review authors were involved in reaching consensus decisions.

canonical_statement: Meta-analyses used a generic inverse-variance fixed-effect model for effect estimates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted meta-analyses using a generic inverse variance fixed-effect model to derive estimates of effect size.

canonical_statement: GRADE methods were used to assess confidence in effect estimates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used GRADE methods to assess our confidence in the effect estimates.

canonical_statement: Four included studies randomized 126 participants; most had Alzheimer disease, with a few participants having vascular or mixed dementia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included four studies (126 participants) in this review. Most participants had Alzheimer's disease; a few had vascular dementia or mixed dementia.

population.label: Participants in four included randomized trials

canonical_statement: Three included trials had crossover designs; interventions lasted 3 to 14 weeks, and one study reported adverse events over 70 weeks of follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Three trials had a cross-over design. Interventions were applied over 3 to 14 weeks; one study reported adverse events over 70 weeks of follow-up.

canonical_statement: Included studies tested natural delta-9-THC (Namisol) and the synthetic THC analogues dronabinol and nabilone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The included studies tested natural delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) (Namisol) and two types of synthetic THC analogue (dronabinol and nabilone).

canonical_statement: Two included studies reported non-commercial funding and two reported both commercial and non-commercial support.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two studies reported non-commercial funding, and two studies were conducted with the support of both commercial and non-commercial funding.

canonical_statement: The review authors declared no conflicts of interest.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The review authors have no conflict of interest to declare.

canonical_statement: The review received NIHR support via Cochrane Infrastructure funding to the Cochrane Dementia and Cognitive Improvement Group.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review was supported by the National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), via Cochrane Infrastructure funding to the Cochrane Dementia and Cognitive Improvement Group.

canonical_statement: The evidence base comprised only four small, short, heterogeneous placebo-controlled trials, limiting certainty and precision.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Based on data from four small, heterogeneous, and short placebo-controlled trials, it is uncertain whether cannabinoids have any beneficial or harmful effects on dementia compared to placebo.

canonical_statement: Applicability was limited because most participants had Alzheimer disease and trials were conducted only in the USA, Canada, and the Netherlands.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most participants had Alzheimer's disease; a few had vascular dementia or mixed dementia. One trial was undertaken in the USA, one in Canada, and two in The Netherlands.

canonical_statement: The review concluded that it remained uncertain whether cannabinoids had beneficial or harmful effects in dementia and that any benefits might be too small to be clinically meaningful.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Based on data from four small, heterogeneous, and short placebo-controlled trials, it is uncertain whether cannabinoids have any beneficial or harmful effects on dementia compared to placebo. If there are benefits of cannabinoids for people with dementia, the effects may be too small to be clinically meaningful.

canonical_statement: The authors called for adequately powered, well-designed trials with adequate dosing, sufficient duration, long-term follow-up, patient-important outcomes, and economic evaluation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our review demonstrates the need for new, well-designed trials to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and economics of cannabinoids for individuals with dementia.
